title: HuginnMindResponse
description:
Every answer a mind gives. A refusal is data in the response, never a
transport failure: the read side carries `Refused`, the write side carries
the outcome's own `Refused`.

oneOf.description:
The answer did not fit one send and is being held for the client to
fetch. Nothing in a mind produces this: the daemon's serve module does,
in place of an answer, and the answer it stands for is the named
MessagePack of the `HuginnMindResponse` the mind gave.

AdmissionFacts.description:
What admission recorded about a document when it landed: the receipt that
wrote it, the `now` that receipt was taken at, who asked, and the
receipt's ordinal, which is the read side's order and its snapshot
position.

CitationRole.description:
The referring field of a citation edge, one per leaf field that names
another document. The wire spelling is the field's own name, so a client
reads an edge's role as the field it came from.

DeferredAnswer.description:
Where the body of an answer that did not fit one send can be fetched: the
reference's own manifest, whose `contentHash` is the SHA-256 of the answer's
encoded bytes and whose chunks are asked for, one at a time, on the session
this arrived on. Row-level facts come from asking again with a header
projection; there is no summary.

manifest.description: gamecult.mesh.cdn_artifact_manifest.v1, the C# reference's CultMeshCdnArtifactManifest as its positional array: [artifactId, kind, version, contentHash, sizeBytes, mimeType, createdAtUtc, chunks[[chunkHash, offset, sizeBytes, recordKey]], tags, metadata].

Faculty.description:
Which faculty a batch was admitted as. Attribution, not authority
(ruling 18): no admission rule trusts it, and Cut 9's views read it back
from the receipt.

ForeignRef.description: A citation of a document in another repo's pipeline store (D6).

FullSha.description: A full git commit id: exactly 40 lowercase hex characters.

ImportSource.description:
The receipt a batch replays and the mind it came from: a quotation of the source receipt, which
stays the primary record. `faculty`, `agent`, `session` and `tool` are the source's, the batch's
own being the importer's. `external` lists the referents the batch cites that this mind does not
hold and does not import: each is treated as in force and nothing reads its content.

IndexStatus.description:
How far the semantic index has caught up with the mind. The mind decides
none of it: the daemon's index worker reports it, in memory, and a restart
recomputes it. `pending` counts documents not yet known to be in the index.

oneOf.description: The worker has not yet compared the mind with the collection.
Every indexable document is in the collection.
Reconciled, and indexing what is still pending.

The last attempt failed (the embedder or the vector store is
unreachable, or refused); it is retried with a backoff and nothing is
dropped. `attempts` counts consecutive failures.

The collection belongs to another writer. The worker never recreates
it; it re-reads it on the same backoff.

LandedName.description: A name the cut landed, and where it lives.

Line.description: Text of at most 1,000 UTF-8 bytes.

MemoryOrigin.description:
Where a Persona turn's batch came from and whom she heard it from: a
memory's origin and a brief's. The organ derives it from the batch of the
turn; the model never writes it.
`about` names whom a memory concerns, this names the room and the voices.

oneOf.description: A turn in rooms: their aliases comma-joined, and the batch's other senders.

A direct message: the DM's room id, and the others who spoke in it (whom
she heard it from in confidence).
A wake: no one spoke.
A Self run of hers, by its label.
Her Sleep run, by its label: a memory she formed in her night.

MindRefusal.description:
Every way a mind refuses. `Document` wraps the leaf's four (bounds,
formats, key identity, foreign type); the rest are the organ's: store
identity, epoch, ownership, batch shape, references, and every cross-field
and cross-document rule of admission.

The two sequenced kinds refuse in the same pair of shapes: an
`OutOfSequence` when the writer's `sequence` is not the previous plus one,
and `AlreadyResolved`/`AlreadyStewarded` when a record of that scope is
still in force.

oneOf.description: A consolidation and the supersession of the memory it consumes come together: `memory` consolidates `consumed`, or is named as superseding it, without the other half in the batch.
`campaign` names the refused document: a campaign, or a target revision that empties its predecessor's repos.
`campaign` moved to mind `to`: nothing is written under its root here any more, whoever asks.
A campaign moves to another mind, never to the one that gives it up.
A Moved resolution is final; withdrawing it would leave two minds keeping the campaign.
An import names this mind as its source.
An import carries a document of `root`, which is no campaign this mind holds or the batch carries, or which this mind holds a native write under.
An import lists `id` as external, but this mind (or the batch) holds it.

The persona document fails the published schema: `path` is the
document location (a key the schema does not declare is `*`) and
`message` the schema keyword that failed. Never the offending value.

The document's `personaId` is not this mind's instance, which is
`instance`.

The put's `expected_updated_at` is not the stored document's
`updatedAt`, which is `stored` (none when no persona is stored).

The document's `provenance.authority` is not `canonical`: a projection
or an import is not the mind's persona.

A run claims work another run in force already holds: `item` is the
claimed document's id and `run` the id of the run that holds it.

A run of hers opens, or is reinstated, while another in-force run of
hers of the same instance and turn is live: `run` is the holder's id
(ruling one-live-self-run).

The one refusal a mind never raises: the answer exceeds the largest
body the organ will deliver by any plane, one send or a deferred body.
It lives here because a refusal rides the response schema and there is
one of those, so a client reads it the way it reads every other refusal
rather than parsing a second vocabulary. `bytes` is the encoded answer
(the payload, not its envelope) and `limit` is the largest body the
daemon defers, both so a caller can narrow its own request; nothing is
truncated or paginated on its behalf. The daemon owns it and its
deferral bound decides it; no rule of the mind is involved.

A selection the substrate or the organ's value door refused: `field`
is the selection field the client sent, `value` the offending part.

A cursor that does not decode, does not belong to this selection or
was not minted by this process, or names a snapshot this mind has not
reached.

MindStatus.description: What a mind says about itself: the typed state a dashboard projects.

documents.description:
Pipeline documents in the image; the epoch record and the receipts are
not documents and are not counted here.

persona.description: The persona door as `PersonaGet` would find it.

MutationRecord.description:
One mutation a report ran: a key-safe label a verdict claim can name,
the exact edit, and the tree it was applied to.

OpenPr.description: A pull request open on the forge.

OrgRepo.description:
A GitHub repository as `Org/Repo`, at most 140 UTF-8 bytes (39 + 1 +
100). The owner is 1 to 39 `[A-Za-z0-9-]` bytes with no leading or
trailing hyphen; the repo is 1 to 100 `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` bytes, is never
`.` or `..`, and does not end in `.git`, ASCII-case-insensitively.
Identity is case-insensitive: `GameCult/Epiphany` and `gamecult/epiphany`
are the same repository.

Para.description: Text of at most 4,000 UTF-8 bytes; longer narrative is cited by `DocRef`.

PersonaPutOutcome.description: How a put ended. A refusal is an answer, as for `admit`.

PersonaStateView.description:
What `PersonaGet` answers: the stored document, its `updatedAt`, and the
receipt of the put that wrote it.

PersonaStatus.description:
What the persona door holds, in the one vocabulary the door itself answers
in: nothing yet, a document with this `updatedAt`, or a stored document the
door cannot read (`PersonaGet` and every put answer `Unavailable`).

PipelineAdmissionOutcome.description:
How admission ended. `Committed.writes` names every document the batch
landed, derived writes included; Cut 11 indexes from it after `admit`
returns, and never inside it.

PipelineDocument.description:
The envelope enum, adjacently tagged on the kind name: a document
on a wire is `{ kind, value }`, and `kind` is exactly what
`PipelineKind::name()` returns, so a reader dispatches on the kind
segment it already knows from the key and needs no second registry
mapping variant spellings to kinds. Adjacent rather than internal
because a value is a named map of its own and an internal tag would
have to be merged into it; the tag stays beside the value instead.
This is not a published schema: `schemas/cultnet` publishes the
eighteen per-kind value documents, and the envelope is the wire's
shape, not a document's.

PipelineDocumentSummary.description:
The organ's meaning of `projection: header`: a document's id, the facts of
its admission, its status and the few fields of its kind a caller triages
by. Derived per read and bounded by `SUMMARY_MAX_BYTES`.

PipelineDocumentView.description:
One document as a reader gets it: its id, the document, the facts of its
admission and its status. The id travels with the document because a
`PipelineDocument` does not carry its key and a client must never derive
one.

PipelineEdge.description:
One citation edge a hop traversed: the organ's typing of the substrate's
edge, whose ends are record keys and whose role is a string.

PipelineFacts.description:
The triage fields of each kind, in the leaf's own envelope spelling. Prose
(`Para`) and unbounded lists are not carried; `finding.claim` and
`follow_up.item` are, because the leaf typed them as one-line statements.

origin.description: Where the Persona turn that admitted it was asked; absent on follow-ups no turn admitted.

PipelineFollowUp.description:
A follow-up. `origin` is where the Persona turn that admitted it was
asked, as the organ derived it: a brief records the conversation whose
message started it. Absent on follow-ups no Persona turn admitted and
on briefs admitted before it existed.

PipelineHandOff.description:
A reassignment of stewardship, recorded in both minds. `documents` names
what travels with it.

PipelineIdea.description:
One thing that could be, including options rejected and ideas no cut
uses yet. `rests_on` is what it stands on (a reader selects the ideas
resting on a stale note with `cites`); `toward` is the fork, ruling or
follow-up it was made for, and empty is legal. It stores no status:
taken up is its Deferred resolution, rejected its Recorded one.
Campaign-rooted: `<campaign>:idea:<pass>.<label>`.

PipelineInstance.description:
A mind's identity document. A store is canonical to exactly one
instance, and this says which; identity lives in the state, not in a
path.

PipelineMemory.description:
One thing a Mind keeps for herself, in her own mind: what she was asked,
decided, committed to, learned or did, an idea, or the rapport between
her and another Mind or person. `text` is her own words. `about` names
the Matrix users it concerns (Minds included) and nothing about where it
came from; `origin` is where and from whom she learned it, and `sources`
the event ids, commits or documents it rests on; the organ fills both,
not the model. `salience_permille` ranks it and decides nothing.
`consolidates` names the memories a consolidating memory replaces.
Instance-rooted: the key is `<instance>:memory:<label>`.

PipelinePageItems.description: The items of a page, chosen once by the selection's `projection`.

PipelineProvenance.description:
Who admitted a batch: the faculty, the agent, its session and the tool.
A field on the receipt and nothing else; the digest excludes it.

imported_from.description:
Set when the batch replays another mind's receipt: the source it quotes. Absent on every
other admission, and then absent from the stored receipt too.

PipelinePulse.description:
One Mind's heartbeat vote, in her own mind: the beat she wants (the swarm's
tempo is the lower median of every Mind's newest vote), the withdrawal of
her standing vote (`tempo_vote_withdrawn`, an explicit null: she counts as
silent again), and the urgency she declares for herself until her next
Persona turn. A pulse says at least one of the three; a withdrawal and a
beat are never both. Instance-rooted: the key is `<instance>:pulse:<label>`, the label
time-ordered like a run's.

PipelineRef.description:
A reference to another document. The id is parsed as a full pipeline id of
the declared `kind`, so the kind and the id's kind segment cannot disagree.

PipelineRefusal.description:
Typed refusals of the pipeline documents: bounds, formats and key identity
(D2's document half), and `ForeignStore`, raised by `decode` for an
envelope of any other type. This is every refusal the leaf decides; a
store's identity and its schema epoch are not decided here, since this
crate owns no store, and belong to the organ that will admit these
documents.

Serialised externally tagged, serde's default for an enum: each variant is
a one-key map from the variant's name to its named fields, so `field` and
`value` are on the wire under their own names and a reader of a refusal
carried over a wire reads the same parts a local caller matches on. No
attribute buys that, which is why there is none: an internal or adjacent
tag would move the fields under a content key without making any of them
more visible.

PipelineReply.description:
One result of her Self session, as its actuator heard it: the words her
Self ended a turn with, and the follow-ups (briefs) the turn answers.
Instance-rooted: the key is `<instance>:reply:<label>`. Not semantically
indexed. Whether the run is hers is admission's rule.

PipelineResearch.description:
One claim a pass found, with the sources it stands on, grouped by `pass`.
What is so, never what to do: a recommendation is an idea. `inferred`
marks a claim read from its sources rather than seen in them. It stores
no status: whether a note is current, superseded or wrong is its
resolutions'. `serves` names the question, cut or campaign document it
was gathered for. The pass's method and what it did not search is its
first note, labelled `scope`. Campaign-rooted:
`<campaign>:research:<pass>.<label>`.

PipelineResolution.description:
The record of how a subject was closed and by what. `sequence` is per
subject and set by the writer, `1` for the first, and it is the last
part of the key, so a subject's resolutions share a prefix and a
withdrawn one is kept under its subject rather than overwritten.
Whether a sequence is the previous plus one, and whether an earlier
resolution still stands, are admission's rules: this crate refuses
neither `0` nor a gap, exactly as it refuses neither `revision: 0` nor
a `revision` with no predecessor.

PipelineRun.description:
One launch of a Self or a Persona turn: the one record of what it took
on. `claims` are the work it holds, and a claim is live while its run
has no resolution in force. `budget_usd` is a canonical decimal string,
`0` for an interactive run. Instance-rooted like stewardship: the key
is `<instance>:run:<label>`. Whether a claim is free is admission's rule.

PipelineSelectionPage.description:
One page of a selection. `matched` is the count before paging, `as_of` the
snapshot the page and every cursor of its walk are exact as of, `edges`
is present exactly when the selection follows a hop, and `scores` exactly
when the answer is semantic: one cosine similarity per item, in order
(higher is nearer), for display and thresholding. It is never stored.

PipelineStatus.description:
Whether a document still stands, and if not, what closed it. Derived at
read time; no document carries a status field and no admission writes one.
The whole closing record travels, not only its outcome, because a reader
rehydrating wants why.

PipelineStatusSummary.description:
Whether a summarised document stands: the closing record's outcome, not its
rationale. A caller who wants why opens the resolution.

PipelineStewardship.description:
Stewardship over a repo, as an assignment recorded in a mind. One
instance may steward several repos, so the repo is part of the key.
`sequence` is per `(instance, repo)`, set by the writer, `1` for the
first, so a repo transferred away and back is two records under one
prefix rather than one document overwriting the other. `assigned_on`
is a field, not a key part. As on a resolution, whether the sequence
is the previous plus one, and which assignment is in force, are
admission's rules and not this crate's.
`names` are the chat names that address her for this repo, matched exactly
as written; none means the repo's own name, matched in any case.

PipelineTarget.description:
`repos`, when non-empty, is the campaign's whole repo set from this
revision on; empty keeps the previous set (ruling campaign-repo-set-home).

PipelineThought.description:
One tick of her stream of thought, offline: the words a base model
continued from a projection of her own state, with the whole trace that
made them (the seed, the projection, every candidate and how near each
was to her earlier thoughts). `text` is the chosen candidate. `reads`
are the documents the seed was drawn from. A thought is divergence for
delivery to weigh, never a memory: its words reach a later seed only
through something she wrote. Instance-rooted: the key is
`<instance>:thought:<label>`, the label `t<unix seconds>` of the tick.
Semantically indexed on `text` only. `nearest_permille` is 1000 where she
had no earlier thought. `prompt_version` names the fixed parts of both
prompts (the Projector's builder revision, guidance and word budget, and
the continuer's frame), so the exact prompts of an old thought can be
rebuilt from the trace.

PrAction.description:
What a pull-request event did. The words are the forge's op names, nothing
a person wrote.

Promise.description:
A promise a report makes about what it landed. Not a document and not
resolvable: it is identified by its report's id and its label, as a
`TargetInvariant` is by its target's. Soul measures every one (ruling
A), and the rule that every one is measured is admission's.

ReadAnchor.description: Code Hands must see but not change, in the spec's repo at the spec's base.

RepoActivity.description:
The answer to an activity read. `events` are other people's changes only,
the asker's own login already dropped, and on a read with no `after` only
those of the last 72 hours: the reader filters nothing again. `head` is the
newest feed id the read saw in those repos, whether or not any event
survived the filter, an entry older than the window too: the cursor to ask
`after` next. `capped` names the repos whose feed the read stopped reading at its page limit: their older entries were not read.
`open_prs` comes only on a read with no `after`; `unseen` and `moved` come on every read, because a repo can go dark in the middle of a session.

moved.description: Of those, the ones whose feed answered a redirect to the forge's own feed route for another repo. The redirect is not followed; a `Location` that is anything else names nothing.

unseen.description: Repos asked about that the anonymous read cannot see: their feed answered 404 or a redirect, and on a read with no `after` the org listing does not hold them either. A repo the listing holds whose feed is dark, and a read with an `after` in which every repo is dark, are not told here: they fail the read.

RepoChange.description:
What an event was. No field carries text a person wrote: a title, a comment
or a commit message is another person's word and has no place here.

oneOf.description: A push to the repo's default branch of `commits` commits.

RepoEvent.description: One thing someone else did in a repo of the asker's.

actor.description: The forge login that did it.

id.description: The forge's own monotonic feed id.

RepoMoved.description: A redirect the forge answered for a repo's feed: it points at `to`.

oneOf.description: A pinned file range in a repo.
A page read on the web: its address, the work it belongs to, and when.
A command, probe, read or capture the pass ran itself.
Another document in the mind.

ResolutionOutcome.description:
How a subject was resolved. Every referent is a parsed `PipelineRef`, so a
resolution names its records by ids of the kinds they declare, validated
where every other referent is; a `Fixed` commit is a `Sha` whose referent
is outside the document set (ruling B). Whether a named document exists,
and how many may supersede one subject, are admission's rules.

oneOf.description:
Overturned, in whole or in part, by later records. The list is bounded
here because the enum is outside `value_types!`, the only place a list
maximum is emitted automatically.

How a Sleep run ended when the ledger took her reply: `line` is her one line, `day_through` the last memory
of her day she was shown (none when the day was empty). It is the one place a night's cut line is kept.

A campaign's history left this mind for `to`, the mind that now keeps it. Final: the campaign and every
document under its root read resolved by this and take no further writes here.

RootTouched.description:
A root of the mind and the newest admission under it. `repos` is the repo set in force of a root that is an in-force campaign,
and empty for any other root.

RunId.description:
The id of a run: a full pipeline id of kind Run. A refusal that names a
holder carries one, so a reader gets a run's id from the wire only if it
parses as one; a peer cannot fill it with any other string. The only ways
in are `TryFrom<String>`, which every deserialized value passes, and the
admission rules, which name a run the mind holds. The error is a fixed
message: it never echoes the offered value.

Sha.description: A git commit id: 7-40 lowercase hex characters.

Sha256Hex.description: A SHA-256 digest: exactly 64 lowercase hex characters.

Short.description: Text of at most 200 UTF-8 bytes.

Slug.description: A campaign slug or key segment: label parts joined by `.`.

SourceHit.description:
One chunk the index holds, as the index holds it: the repo it belongs to,
the path in that repo, the commit whose blob it was cut from, its 1-based
inclusive line range, and its text.

SourceHits.description: The answer to a source search, nearest first.

SourceModel.description:
The model a source collection was built under, and so the one a query must
be embedded by. The address of the embedder is no part of it.

Symbol.description:
A name the location's lines must contain as written there (an
identifier or a YAML `&fileID`); not an identity. 1 to 128 bytes, no
whitespace and no control character.

Title.description:
A title: 1 to 200 UTF-8 bytes, enforced by admission; JSON Schema
length counts characters. Holds at least one alphanumeric character,
no control character, and no bidi control character (`U+061C`,
`U+200E`, `U+200F`, `U+202A`-`U+202E`, `U+2066`-`U+2069`).

VerdictClaim.description:
The promise this claim measured, and the report's mutations it ran. An
`Unproven` claim with a promise is one Soul could not reach.
